title: Hosting tradeoffs playbook for POC: staged pathways and runbook
content:
Context:
This is a lightweight playbook capturing the tradeoffs we discussed in the 2025-10 POC workshop and the recommended staged approach for customers evaluating hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes. Focus is on quick POC velocity while preserving realistic production constraints (security, SLA, cost). Intended audience: SEs, customer infra leads, SREs, and the product manager who will sign off on rollouts.

Summary recommendation (one-liner):
Start with Hosted API for dev velocity + early integration tests, transition to Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost control at scale, and only move to Private when customer requirements demand VPC/on-prem isolation or specific KMS/HSM integrations. Provide a clear canary -> scale -> migrate checklist to reduce risk.

Decision axes (quick reference):
- Latency sensitivity: p50/p95 targets and regional residency
- Data sensitivity: PII/regulated data vs transient telemetry
- Throughput predictability: bursty vs steady high qps
- Cost model preference: pay-as-you-go vs committed capacity
- Ops ownership: customer ops vs Redwood managed
- Compliance & integrations: KMS/HSM, audit logs, network controls

Example thresholds we used in workshop:
- Interactive UI use cases: target p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms
- Batch/analytics hits: throughput 200-2,000 r/s, relaxed p95
- Regulatory: data residency + customer KMS required => Private recommended
- Breakeven (rule of thumb): sustained 1.2M tokens/day or consistent 50-100 GPU-hours/month often favors Dedicated pricing after discounts

Staged pathway (recommended playbook):
1) Sandbox & integration (0-2 weeks):
   - Mode: Hosted API (shared infra)
   - Goals: API integration, prompt engineering, basic observability wiring (traces, errors, token metrics)
   - Must-haves: service account with RBAC, dataset anonymization for sample prompts, baseline latency/cost capture route
   - Risks: no private KMS, potential cold-start variance in p95 during heavy test windows

2) Canary Dedicated (2-6 weeks):
   - Mode: Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) in customer-preferred region
   - Goals: validate throughput, SLOs at target scale, run synthetic load with KV cache warmups
   - Work: provisioning ticket to infra (JIRA INF-789), add autoscale policy with burst headroom, test graceful fallback to hosted variant
   - Metrics to capture: tokens/sec, cost per 1000 tokens, cache hit rate, tail latency under steady vs spike traffic

3) Private evaluation (4-12+ weeks):
   - Mode: Private control plane (VPC) or on-prem package when required
   - Goals: audit logs end-to-end, KMS integration, firewall whitelisting, legal review and SOC documentation
   - Longer lead times: network peering, customer infra readiness, HSM approvals

Routing and resilience patterns (ops checklist):
- Smart routing policy: routes by priority (latency-critical -> Dedicated -> Hosted fallback).
- Canary routing: 5% traffic to new pool, 25% after 24h stable, 100% after 72h and no regression alerts.
- Fallback policy: auto-failover to hosted variant when GPU utilization > 85% or error rate > 1% for 5m.
- Cache priming: ensure prefix/KV cache populated by synthetic runs before cutover.

Security & compliance notes:
- Hosted: great for rapid POCs, limited to Redwood-managed KMS, standard audit logs. Not suitable where customer-managed KMS is mandatory.
- Dedicated: supports dedicated tenancy and stronger isolation; we still recommend encrypted transports and RBAC.
- Private: required for customers needing customer KMS/HSM, air-gapped review, or specific legal clauses.

Cost modeling snapshot (back-of-envelope):
- Hosted: $0.XX per 1k tokens (varies by model). Low upfront, high variable cost if usage scales.
- Dedicated: committed monthly $M for pool + lower per-token compute. Better at sustained load.
- Private: license/installation fee + customer infra costs. Capital-light for Redwood but heavy for customer ops.

POC runbook (actionable checklist):
- Pre-work (SE): agree SLOs, ensure test data anonymized, get contacts for customer networking and security.
- Day 0: create API keys, configure basic dashboard capture (token metrics + latency), confirm alerting channels.
- Week 1: run integration smoke tests, record sample prompts and reference outputs for quality baseline.
- Week 2-4: if throughput goals unmet, request Dedicated pilot. Run cache warmup + synthetic spiky test (emailed schedule to customer ops).
- During Dedicated pilot: track cost vs latency, capture model variant regressions (tie to prompt set), plan rollback window.
- Private signoff gates: legal/compliance checklist completed, KMS integration tested, networking validated, support SLA agreed.

Open questions / unresolved items from last workshop:
- Customer asked for cold-start mitigation guarantees — we should propose a cache-warming runbook and documented warm-up SLAs. Owner: Samir (JIRA:SE-452).
- Need clearer break-even calculator for Dedicated vs Hosted (inputs: token distribution, concurrency). Action: finance/solutions to draft a one-pager with examples. Owner: Rosa.
- On-prem packaging compatibility with customer HSM (vendor X) — infra team to validate driver compatibility. Owner: Luca.

Risks & mitigations quicklist:
- Risk: Customer data policy prevents sending prompts to hosted environment. Mitigation: Start POC with masked/anonymized data; expedite Dedicated/Private evaluation path.
- Risk: Early cost surprises on hosted API during high-volume tests. Mitigation: enforce quota limits and cost alerts, or use dedicated prepaid pool for load tests.
- Risk: Network onboarding delays for Private. Mitigation: perform network pre-checks and request network diagram + firewall rules before formal kickoff.

Appendix: short template to include in customer proposal email
- Objective: Validate integration + SLOs for feature X using Redwood inference.
- Phase 1: Hosted integration (2 weeks) — low friction, quick feedback loop.
- Phase 2: Dedicated pilot (4 weeks) — throughput & cost validation.
- Phase 3: Private (optional) — compliance & KMS.
- Deliverables: baseline latency report, cost delta analysis, recommended deployment mode and migration checklist.

Notes to self / SE tips:
- Bring a curated set of 8–12 prompts for quality regression checks (store them as a shared gist).
- Pre-author a rollback playbook for canary failures (how to shift traffic back and token budget considerations).
- Keep communication with customer security tight — share SOC docs early.

-- end --
